statement: Two of the prior x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md scout digest's tool characterizations were factually wrong for codebase-memory-mcp v0.8.1, verified by full line-by-line reads of the C handlers: (1) ingest_traces (src/mcp/mcp.c:5567-5597) is an unimplemented stub — it parses the traces array only to count its length, never reads caller/callee/count, never touches the store, and returns {"status":"accepted","traces_received":N,"note":"Runtime edge creation from traces not yet implemented"}; there is no merge-into-CALLS-edges behavior of any kind to port. (2) detect_changes (mcp.c:5215-5383) has NO risk classification scheme at all — grepped the full handler plus src/pipeline/pass_gitdiff.c for risk/CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with zero matches; the CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW hop-distance risk-label scheme that exists in this codebase belongs exclusively to trace_path's risk_labels param (mcp.c §5.3 of the doc). detect_changes's own `depth` param is read, clamped via the shared clamp_mcp_depth/cbm_mcp_max_depth (default 15, override CBM_MCP_MAX_DEPTH), and echoed into the response — but is never actually used to bound anything; detect_add_impacted_symbols only looks up symbols defined directly in each changed file, no BFS/multi-hop expansion despite the depth-shaped param.
why: A digest/summary-level description of a tool's shape (written from a name+schema without reading the handler body) can silently encode a feature that does not exist, or invent behavior for a dead parameter. Implementers porting to Rust who trust the digest over the source would build risk-classification logic and trace-merge logic that has zero baseline to match against, producing parity-harness failures with no baseline artifact to diff against.
howToApply: Before implementing or parity-testing any codebase-memory-mcp tool port, read x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md section for that tool (all 14 tools now fully verified with file:line citations as of this lane) rather than the older x06-source-scout-digests.md summary — where they conflict, the schemas doc's cited-to-source claim wins. Specifically: do not implement CALLS-edge merge semantics for ingest_traces (replicate the stub instead, or treat as new product design if the capability is actually wanted); do not implement a risk-level enum for detect_changes (it doesn't exist in baseline).

evidence.ref: codebase-memory-mcp v0.8.1 shallow clone src/mcp/mcp.c:5567-5597 (ingest_traces), mcp.c:5215-5383 + src/pipeline/pass_gitdiff.c (detect_changes, zero risk-token matches)

statement: codebase-memory-mcp's stdio transport is dual-framing, auto-detected per message, not a single fixed choice: cbm_mcp_server_run (src/mcp/mcp.c:6137-6214) reads one line via cbm_getline; if the line starts with the literal 'Content-Length:' it switches to LSP-style header+body framing for that message (handle_content_length_frame, mcp.c:6041-6070, reply also framed with a Content-Length header); otherwise the line itself IS the JSON-RPC message (newline-delimited JSON, the default MCP-spec path) and the reply is a bare '%s\n'. Separately, the CLI form (cli <tool> <json>) unwraps the MCP content/isError envelope by default — cli_print_mcp_result (src/main.c:208-234) prints only content[0].text (stdout if isError:false, stderr if true) and maps isError to exit code 1 vs 0 — but passing --json bypasses this unwrapping AND stops threading isError into the exit code (main.c:473-474 always leaves exit_code at its default-initialized 0), so a caller scripting against --json output must parse the envelope's isError field itself rather than trusting the process exit code.
why: Both of these are the kind of framing/exit-code detail that is easy to get wrong by assumption (the doc's prior pass had marked stdio framing UNVERIFIED and guessed newline-delimited-only, which was directionally right but incomplete) and directly affects how a Rust reimplementation's stdio loop and CLI wrapper must behave to be wire-compatible.
howToApply: When implementing enforcer-memory's own MCP stdio server or CLI wrapper, replicate the dual-framing auto-detect (peek first line for the Content-Length prefix, else treat as NDJSON) if LSP-client compatibility matters, and mirror the CLI's envelope-unwrap-by-default plus the --json-loses-exit-code-mapping quirk only if byte-for-byte CLI parity is a stated goal — otherwise treat it as a documented baseline wart, not something to copy uncritically.
